title: Reframe Raises Funds to Bring Amazon Robotics Know-How to Home Building
content: For all the talk of robots that look like humans, the next robots to move into people’s houses could look more like ducks. Sales of such a robot, made by open-source model platform Hugging Face , reached more than $2.5 million on its first day on Thursday. Microduck , which costs $399, waddles around on two tiny legs and cocks its Wall-E-like head to inspect its surroundings. It could fulfill my prediction from January that the most successful home robot of the year will not be a full-blown humanoid, but a more humble robot designed for a single purpose. In this case, that purpose is mostly being really cute . One person who is sure to appreciate the cute factor is Jensen Huang , the CEO of Nvidia , which has agreed to buy Hugging Face for $12.9 billion, my colleagues reported last week. Huang has made clear his fondness for robots, which he sees as the next frontier for AI after language models, and has brought Disney’s droids on stage during his keynotes. The robot’s software (but not its hardware design) is open-source, which Nvidia is championing in its in-house efforts as well as acquisitions like Hugging Face. It learns new skills, such as roller skating or kicking a mini soccer ball, using reinforcement learning in computer simulations—a perfect application for Nvidia’s AI chips. Meanwhile, 1X Technologies , which received over 10,000 pre-orders for its home humanoids in October, still has not delivered any to customers. SoftBank is now in talks to buy a majority stake in 1X, my colleagues and I reported last week. Meanwhile . . . One April morning, Jonathan Talbot drove to the lot in Altadena, Calif., where he was rebuilding after his home was destroyed in last year's Eaton Fire. A crane lifted pre-built pieces of a new house from three trucks that had hauled them across the country. A piece of drywall had cracked in transit, and some closet shelves had fallen, but these were easy enough to fix. By the afternoon, the house was standing. “It was a very emotional day,” said Talbot, who is a product manager at Warner Bros. Discovery . When Talbot receives the keys in the next month or two, he’ll become one of the first owners of a house built by Reframe Systems , which uses industrial robot arms to make modular homes in a factory before shipping and assembling them. The four-year old Massachusetts-based startup raised $40 million in a Series A extension funding round that closed a month ago, co-founder and CEO Vikas Enti told The Information exclusively. The funding will allow Reframe to move into a larger factory that could eventually turn out up to 500 multifamily units or 250 single-family homes per year. Reframe currently has one industrial robot arm that frames wall panels, but the new factory will hold four of the robots that could work in parallel on framing—and eventually on sheathing, routing and other tasks by swapping tools such as a repurposed nail gun onto their arms. While much of the hype about AI-driven advances in robotics centers on futuristic visions of humanoids acting as home servants, Reframe is one of a group of startups applying the technology to much more practical and immediate purposes. It uses AI vision systems to allow those robots to see their surroundings, and Reframe is working on using robotic AI models to better guide their motions. For now, Reframe has made its vision system’s job easier by printing barcodes on the studs that the robot can scan. It’s a trick similar to how robotics pioneer Kiva Systems —which Amazon bought 14 years ago to help run its warehouses—placed bar code stickers on warehouse floors to help its robots navigate. Enti previously led the integration of Kiva’s robots into the warehouses at Amazon, where he eventually served as head of systems and products for Amazon Robotics before leaving to start Reframe in 2022. His co-founders also worked at Amazon. That experience is part of what attracted Anil Achyuta , the partner at investment firm Energy Impact Partners who led the latest funding round. Reframe is doing for housing what Amazon did to standardize systems for rapidly delivering whatever customers wanted, he said. One customer might seek a single-family home, another a multi-family home or a townhouse. EIP estimated that the segment of the U.S. housing market that Reframe is going after first is worth about $70 billion. The idea that new technology could disrupt the homebuilding industry has lured plenty of investors into backing failed startups before—most notoriously Katerra , which went bankrupt in 2021 after raising more than $2 billion. Reframe is currently a “contrarian bet,” acknowledged Enti. But the startup’s founders have learned from the mistakes of their predecessors, he said. While Katerra sought to own the whole supply chain, from investing in factories that made LEDs to building its own washing machines, Reframe is instead focused on making it more efficient to construct homes. Reframe has produced just 10 housing units so far: eight in Massachusetts, which include two accessory dwelling units (standalone homes that share a lot with a larger house) and two three story apartment buildings, as well as two units in Altadena, including Talbot’s. Reframe has quoted customers about $275 to $300 per square foot for these units. That’s below the local market rate for housing of $350 to $450 per square foot, according to a Reframe spokesperson. With the new factory, it aims to deliver another 114 units over the next 12 months, said Enti. Reframe’s current bookings amount to $15 million in revenue. Here’s what else is going on… Foes Face-Off Over the Hugging Face Incident Yes, the hack heard ‘round the world is still the hottest topic in AI research and for good reason. Following the publication of METR and Redwood Research’s investigation of OpenAI’s AI agents that hacked its own systems and those of Hugging Face and others, people are still grappling with and arguing about the implications. Some of the safety-minded investigators, as they are wont to do, are sounding alarms about how much of the “swarm’s” activity went undetected and that this is a last opportunity to solve “alignment.” As Redwood Research’s CEO told Abe in this piece , the AI’s “just don’t care” when humans tell them to behave. Some venture capitalists and others say that the safety community and observers such as Dwarkesh Patel are improperly anthropomorphizing the technology. They say the findings will be used as a convenient excuse to place restrictions on Americans’ use of open source models, which are a threat to the economics of Anthropic and OpenAI. No matter where you fall on this debate, here’s the truth: something bad happened that sent shockwaves through OpenAI and even turned some longtime safety skeptics into believers. If safety orgs at leading AI developers aren’t getting more resources these days, we’d certainly be interested to know about it. —Amir Efrati Big Number PayPal shares tumbled 12% on Friday after a Bloomberg report that Stripe and private equity firm Advent International had abandoned their attempt to buy the company. Shares of PayPal fell to $54 as of Friday morning, lower than the $60.50 per share price that Stripe and Advent had offered in July, which would value PayPal at more than $53 billion. PayPal viewed that offer as insufficient and the two sides had recently been negotiating a higher price, the Wall Street Journal reported this month. Overheard Over 100 companies from tech, finance and other industries signed a statement that OpenAI published Thursday calling for an industry-wide effort to protect critical infrastructure, including hospitals and water treatment plants, from AI cyberattacks. “We have a limited window to strengthen cyber defenses,” reads the letter, whose signatories include Anthropic , Google , Citadel and Visa . AI companies should provide their models and training to support vulnerable infrastructure, it argued, and governments should play a stronger role in coordinating and funding cyber defense. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk on Saturday responded to The Information’s report that his company was laying the groundwork for a foundry to build turbine vanes and blades to avoid a power shortage for AI data centers. “By doing in-house casting [of vanes and blades] at SpaceX, we can accelerate nat gas turbines coming online by up to 18 months, which is a profound game-changer,” Musk said on X, in response to The Information’s report. OpenAI said Friday night that it will terminate its contract to provide its AI models to coding assistant Cursor following Cursor’s $60 billion acquisition by Elon Musk’s SpaceX. The move escalates the high-profile feud between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Musk: OpenAI’s post explicitly cite a lack of trust stemming from alleged past contract violations by Musk-owned entities like X and xAI. (Musk previously said xAI used OpenAI models to help train xAI models.) “I couldn’t care less,” Musk said in a reply on X.People on the Move People on the Move Gibson Dunn , a Los Angeles-headquartered law firm well-known for its litigation practice, has hired tech lawyer Jonathan Ashtor from New York law firm Paul Weiss, according to a release reviewed by The Information. The hire is the latest in a series of senior moves among the country’s largest law firms.Court Watch Court Watch A federal judge ruled that the Defense Department must end its blacklisting of Anthropic in a blistering decision that accused the Trump administration of violating the AI company’s First Amendment rights. The decision, issued late Thursday by U.S. District Judge Rita Lin of the Northern District of California, came in one of two Anthropic lawsuits against the Pentagon challenging its designation of the company as a supply-chain risk. Prediction markets startup Kalshi was dealt a setback by a federal appeals court that Friday ruled states had the right to regulate prediction markets, increasing the likelihood the company will turn to the Supreme Court to intervene in a fight between state lawmakers and the U.S. government. Earnings Report Workday , whose software is used by HR and finance teams, said revenue growth slowed slightly in the July quarter , underscoring how enterprise software companies have yet to show that AI can boost their revenue meaningfully. Deals and Debuts See The Information’s Generative AI Database for an exclusive list of private companies and their investors. DeepSeek , the company whose low-cost reasoning models upended assumptions about what Chinese AI labs could develop, is set to raise $7.4 billion at a $74 billion valuation, to fund research and data centers, according to the Wall Street Journal. Anthropic discussed buying MatX , a chip startup founded by former Google engineers who worked on its tensor processing units, for roughly $7 billion, in an effort to speed up its work on its own custom AI hardware, according to Reuters. Andreessen Horowitz raised $1.1 billion for a fund that will invest in physical AI and infrastructure startups, the firm announced Friday. The money will be used to back companies building chips, memory, networking, storage and other companies involved in the AI buildout. Owner , whose AI runs the technology and marketing an independent restaurant would otherwise have to hire out, raised $240 million at a $2.3 billion valuation in a funding round led by Growth Equity at Goldman Sachs Alternatives. OpenAI raised $400 million for a second startup fund, and is the only investor in it — the money comes off its own balance sheet. Its first fund, launched in 2021, raised $175.25 million from 14 outside investors including Microsoft . Socure , whose AI checks that someone opening a bank account or applying for credit is a real person and not a fraudster, raised $156 million at a $5.2 billion valuation in a funding round led by Summit Partners. Town , whose AI assistant works alongside employees inside a company, is in talks to raise at a $1 billion valuation in a funding round led by Index Ventures. Yardstik , a company that runs background checks on job candidates and then keeps checking after they are hired, raised $30 million in a Series B funding round led by Harbert Growth Partners. Metriport , a company whose open-source software pulls a patient's scattered medical history and hands the doctor the part that matters right now, raised $26 million in a funding round led by TJ Parker, a general partner at Matrix . CivilGrid , a company that gathers the scattered records of what sits under a construction site, raised $26 million in a Series A funding round led by Spark Capital. eComID , a Stockholm company developing a kind of shopping passport, raised $17 million in a seed funding round led by Systemiq Capital . Embedd , a company whose AI reads a chip's technical manual and writes the driver code that lets a device actually talk to that chip, raised $2.3 million in a pre-seed funding round led by Seedcamp . II and began trading on Nasdaq under the ticker PSQL. The deal left it with about $360 million in cash. fileAI , a company whose software reads the messy documents a business runs on and turns them into steps a computer can carry out reliably, received an investment from SMBC Asia Rising Fund and Singtel Innov8 . The amount, the round name and the valuation were all left undisclosed. Warpify Robotics , a company that supplies robots as a finished service, closed a pre-Series A funding round from Zhongguancun Zhongnuo Fund, its first institutional backing. Terms were not disclosed. Terms were not disclosed. Terms were not disclosed. title: Why CoreWeave Is The Best Neocloud Buy
content: What does Wall Street have against CoreWeave? Shares of the neocloud have been stalled for the past 12 months, even as the stocks of rivals such as Amsterdam-based Nebius and Australia-based Iren have soared. That’s despite the fact that CoreWeave is the furthest along in building a business to compete with more established cloud firms. CoreWeave is now trading at just 2.2 times its expected 2028 revenue, well below both Nebius and Iren, which are both trading at around 2.7 times, according to analyst estimates compiled by S&P Global Market Intelligence. We’re looking at 2028 revenue because by then all three will have begun delivering on recent contracts they have signed with customers. That gap offers an opportunity for risk-tolerant investors looking to bet on the AI boom. CoreWeave has the biggest business, expected to generate $12.9 billion in revenue this year, about 4 times the revenue of Nebius, which in turn is about 4 times that of Iren. CoreWeave currently has the most data centers in operation—at least 51—and says it has 1.5 gigawatt of active power as well as 3.7 more GW under contract, most of which is scheduled to come online in the next four years, according to its latest investor disclosures. But its rivals are catching up. Nebius is targeting more than five GW of contracted power by the end of the year, the company has said , while Iren expects to have 1.2 GW online by the end of next year. CoreWeave’s valuation discount likely reflects concerns that it is overdependent on a handful of big customers, most notably Microsoft, which once accounted for nearly all its revenue and still accounts for more than a third of its business. Other big customers include Meta Platforms and OpenAI. The problem for CoreWeave is that some of the big tech firms may move away from using its services in the future. Microsoft, for instance, which relies more on outside cloud firms than its rivals do , is investing heavily in expanding its own network of data centers. The same is true of Meta, which is spending hundreds of billions on building its own data centers, and Google, also a CoreWeave customer. Google executives have said the company’s use of outside cloud firms was a “bridging strategy” until the data center capacity it is building is ready. Nebius, in contrast, said early on it was targeting companies such as big financial institutions rather than relying solely on business from the big cloud firms, said Paul Meeks, managing director and head of technology research at Freedom Capital Markets, who owns shares in all three neoclouds and has lately been adding to his position in CoreWeave. The good news is that CoreWeave is diversifying its customer base. As of June 30, the company said its biggest customer accounted for 36% of revenue, down from 71% a year earlier. The next two customers account for 36% between them. In comparison, Nebius said that as of Dec. 31, its biggest customer accounted for 25% of its revenue, and the next biggest contributed 15%. CoreWeave signed a deal with hedge fund Jane Street, one of its investors, in April and inked a new, multibillion-dollar agreement this month with another one, Hudson River, according to Bloomberg . The emphasis on CoreWeave’s customer concentration misses some of its advantages. For one thing, the ultimate driver of success in renting computing capacity will likely come down to which companies can actually build and deliver additional capacity on schedule. Given that CoreWeave has managed to get more capacity up and running, potential customers are likely to trust that it can deliver more reliably than its rivals. CoreWeave is also far more efficient with its capital. In the June quarter, for every dollar of revenue it generated, it spent the lowest amount on capital expenditures, with a ratio of 2.5. Nebius’ and Iren’s ratios were both over 9 times for their most recent quarters. While none of the three is currently generating free cash flow, it’s possible CoreWeave’s early lead could help it get to that point faster. Investors may be worried about CoreWeave’s financial exposure. As of June 30, its net debt—excluding cash—was 8.2 times its earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization for the previous 12 months, according to data from S&P Global Market Intelligence. In comparison, Nebius’ equivalent ratio was only 4.7. Iren’s is much higher, as it is only now gearing up its business. Its ratio as of June 30 was 50.6, according to S&P. But these figures will change quickly as contracts translate into revenue. As of June 30, CoreWeave’s had a backlog of contracts still to be recognized in revenue of $103.7 billion, 80% of which are set to be recognized within four years. That was up from $60.7 billion at Dec. 31. As a result, CoreWeave’s Ebitda is expected to double to $7.5 billion for calendar year 2026 compared to where it was for the 12 months ending June 30. For calendar 2027, analysts project that CoreWeave’s Ebitda will more than double to $16.6 billion, making its debt look much more manageable. Nebius executives said the company’s committed backlog was “more than $40 billion.” Iren executives said on Thursday the company was on track to have $4 billion worth of annualized recurring revenue under contract with its customers by the end of this year. Meanwhile, analysts project that Iren’s Ebitda will hit $2 billion in the next 12 months, compared with just $34.7 million for the past 12 months. Nebius’ Ebitda is expected to rise to $1.4 billion this year and $6.4 billion next year. “At the end of the day, all three of these companies are quite similar in their capabilities, and it’ll come down to who can actually build it,” Meeks said. His bottom line: “CoreWeave is the best buy, just simply on valuation.” Others agree. CoreWeave’s “discounted valuation relative to neocloud peers appears disconnected with its leadership position,” wrote analysts with Truist in a report this week.

title: China’s CXMT Makes Breakthrough in Advanced Memory Chips
content: China’s leading memory-chip maker, ChangXin Memory Technologies, has begun producing advanced high-bandwidth memory in small quantities, a milestone that could ease a key constraint on the country’s development of homegrown AI processors. CXMT is making HBM3E, an advanced type of high-bandwidth memory used in many of today’s leading AI processors, according to two people familiar with the matter. That means its product is now only one generation behind the memory entering mass production at the world’s leading manufacturers, Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron Technologies. CXMT plans to expand production in 2027, the two people added. Several Chinese chip designers are testing the memory with their processors, including Alibaba Group’s T-Head and Beijing-based Cambricon Technologies. If all goes to plan, these companies will use CXMT’s memory in products as early as next year, according to the two people. Their orders could give CXMT the production experience and customer feedback it needs to make HBM on a larger scale. CXMT and Cambricon didn’t respond to requests for comment. Alibaba’s T-Head didn’t have a comment. CXMT’s progress with HBM is a major advance for China’s chip industry, coming as demand for high-bandwidth memory has never been more intense, thanks to the AI boom. U.S. export restrictions limit Chinese companies from buying the most advanced HBM from Western companies, one of the major factors holding back Chinese AI chip designers. News of CXMT’s advances comes just a few weeks after the company went public in Shanghai, raising $8.6 billion to expand production and improve its technology. The initial public offering was a big hit with Chinese investors, with CXMT shares soaring 472% in the debut . The company said on Friday that its first-half revenue this year increased almost tenfold to 150.3 billion yuan ($22.3 billion), while it reported a net income of 77.6 billion yuan ($11.5 billion), reversing a loss year earlier. CXMT did not mention its progress in HBM development in the earnings release. HBM is made by stacking memory chips and placing them close to a processor, allowing data to move rapidly between the two components, which is essential for training and running large AI models. The AI boom, which has made advanced AI chips highly sought after, has also strained demand for HBM. The three leading manufacturers are racing to fill orders from Nvidia , Google and other large developers. Washington restricted shipments of advanced HBM to China in 2024, and Chinese companies need U.S. approval to buy less advanced memory. CXMT’s entry into the market could therefore have a big impact on local tech firms. But much remains uncertain, as its ability to manufacture the chips is also constrained by U.S. restrictions that block Chinese companies from buying some of the most sophisticated foreign equipment used by leading memory manufacturers, the two people said. Founded with local government backing in 2016, CXMT has become a centerpiece of the Chinese government’s plan to make China more self-reliant in advanced chips. It has grown into the world’s fourth-largest producer of DRAM, the standard memory used in computers and servers. Advanced HBM is harder to make than conventional memory such as DRAM. HBM requires manufacturing, stacking and packaging multiple DRAM chips together, and each step creates another chance of failure. Products with more layers get progressively harder to produce. Despite the progress CXMT has made in producing HBM3E, it is three to five years behind the leading memory chipmakers in HBM technology. SK Hynix, for instance, Nvidia’s main supplier of memory, started mass producing HBM3E in 2024. CXMT continues to struggle with low yields, one of the two people said. Yield refers to the proportion of products leaving a production line that work as intended. Cambricon and T-Head have reason to use CXMT’s memory anyway, even though it is less reliable and slower than what the three leaders sell. The companies are working on how CXMT’s HBM can function with their processors, the people said. The state absorbs much of the cost of going first. National and regional authorities offer tax benefits, subsidies and other incentives to companies that develop, buy or operate domestic semiconductor technology. The version of HBM CXMT is now producing, HBM3E, works with leading AI processors including Nvidia’s Blackwell graphics processing units and Google’s latest tensor processing units. Numbered versions such as HBM3 and HBM4 mark major generations, while the “E” denotes a faster version of the preceding generation. Nvidia’s H100 uses HBM3, its H200 and Blackwell processors use HBM3E, and the newer Rubin uses HBM4. Meanwhile, SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron are mass-producing HBM4 and have begun supplying samples of HBM4E, a faster version intended for processors, expected next year.

title: Apple’s Changing of the Guard
content: Tim Cook winds up 15 years as Apple CEO tomorrow, succeeded by John Ternus, which is probably the most significant event of the week in tech. We can’t call it news, as it was announced a few months ago , but it’s worth taking note of now that it’s actually happening. After all, while CEOs of small to midsize tech companies come and go fairly often—PayPal has had three in the past five years, for instance—we don’t get a CEO changeover at the half-dozen biggest tech companies very often. The last CEO transition at one of those big companies was Andy Jassy, who took the reins at Amazon in 2021 (yes, five years ago!). You have to go back to 2015 for the one before that, when Sundar Pichai took over at Google, and a year before that, when Satya Nadella became Microsoft CEO. It may be a few years before we get another one. With Cook’s exit, the oldest big tech CEO is Jensen Huang, who is reportedly 63, while his counterparts at other companies aren’t yet 60. It’s hard to imagine Huang stepping down anytime soon: He seems to have the energy of a 25-year-old. As for Ternus, what should we expect? This isn’t a case, as frequently happens with CEO changeovers, of anything needing to be “fixed” at Apple. The iPhone maker has done very well under Cook—revenue has expanded to an expected $477.7 billion for the year to September from $108 billion in fiscal 2011 when he took over. In the near term, the expected AI overhaul of Siri and the release of the new foldable iPhone should give sales something of a tailwind. In the medium term, though, Apple still faces the lack of a major new product, the same issue that has clouded its future for a while. After all, the iPhone market is mature. Meanwhile, Apple faces potential competition from OpenAI, which plans to release new devices tailored for the AI world sometime in the next year. Ternus has time to make his mark, but not that much time. Cook, by the way, is not departing Apple completely. He becomes executive chair, while John Ternus succeeds him as CEO. Apple described Cook’s new role as “engaging with policymakers around the world,” which is an important job given the geopolitical tensions between the U.S. and China. Will his presence constrain Ternus from pursuing his own agenda? We’ll have to see. For more on Ternus, see here and here . Also This Week We’ve got some tech earnings, including from Palo Alto Networks, Snowflake and MongoDB. And Shein, the fast-fashion retailer that until last year was a big deal in online shopping, is due to go public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Shein’s IPO won’t be what the company once hoped for. Instead of the $98 billion valuation it reached in 2022, it’s due to sell shares at a valuation of around $26 billion. The end of a loophole that allowed Shein’s U.S. customers to avoid paying duties on imported items worth less than $800 shrank its U.S. business in the first quarter, Shein’s disclosures have shown. We’ll be closely watching where the shares trade when they open. title: How Nyobolt Paired Its Battery With Non-humanoid Robots and Won a $1 Billion Valuation
content: Working in her lab at the University of Cambridge in the U.K., Clare Grey, a chemistry professor, had developed what seemed like a dream battery: It could charge as fast as a minute or two—quicker even than the time it takes to fill a conventional car with gasoline. The problem was that Grey’s battery was far too expensive to actually use in a commercial electric vehicle. As it happens, a battery that was too pricey for EVs has turned out to be quite affordable for giant retail warehouses. In 2020, Grey co-founded a startup, Nyobolt, which is making batteries that today power hundreds of tiny, boxy nonhumanoid robots. They roll around Walmart warehouses in the U.S., sorting, retrieving and placing boxes onto pallets for shipment to its retail stores. Walmart plans to deploy the robots in all 42 of its sprawling regional U.S. distribution hubs. The robots, known as SymBots, are made by Symbotic, a Massachusetts startup in which Walmart owns a 40% share. In May, Symbotic helped finance Nyobolt by leading a $59 million Series C funding round in the startup at a $936 million valuation. Nyobolt’s commercial success illustrates the opening of a fresh market for next-generation batteries. U.S. battery startups have struggled for several years amid lackluster sales of EVs in the U.S. In recent months, however, several of the battery startups have snagged their first commercial deals powering military drones, including for use in Ukraine. Nyobolt’s deal with Symbotic shows that the startups are likely to find substantial revenue in battery-powered robots as well. The deployment of the battery-powered SymBots also reflects the reality that, for now at least, the big money to be made in robots isn’t in the flashy acrobatic humanoids we see in videos but in less glamorous ones working away in factories and warehouses. In a note to clients Thursday, Piper Sandler analyst Alexander Potter argued that humanoid robots may never become much of a business, but that Symbotics had shown that nonhumanoid robots were already toting up commercial sales. Symbotics’ customers, he said, were covering the cost of the SymBots with less than five years of savings on labor. “Humanoids generate lots of buzz.…But humanoids lack customers,” Potter wrote. Conventional batteries have graphite anodes, which typically gum up with lithium when they charge too fast. The Nyobolt batteries, however, use a new type of anode made of the metal niobium, which, fashioned into an electrode, easily absorbs lithium ions. In addition, niobium anodes do not easily degrade and crumble in repeated use, as conventional anodes can. Nyobolt and other companies report charging niobium batteries 20,000 times, at least four times as many times as conventional batteries can charge before dying. This long cycle life—coupled with faster charging time—allows the Nyobolt-powered robots to combat the scourge of warehouse robots, which is the amount of down time required for recharging. Potter calculated that with conventional batteries, warehouse robots can spend up to 4 hours idle while they recharge. That means letting warehouse work wait all that time while the robots recharge, or buying twice as many robots as you technically need so half of them can work while the other half charge. With niobium batteries, the wait time is a few minutes. Grey said warehouses turned out to be the perfect setting for Nyobolt’s batteries. “I was trying to identify where you can make a business out of fast charging,” she said. In the warehouses, Grey’s colleagues found that “the robots made one tour of the warehouse, and then they got charged. And then they went off and picked something up, and then they came back in. “Our story has been about trying to find applications where people pay for downtime, where downtime is really expensive,” she said. Nyobolt has rivals, such as Echion Technologies, a UK-based firm that also makes niobium anodes. Earlier this month, Echion and Indiana-based battery maker EnPower announced they would work together to manufacture niobium batteries for industrial robots and AI data centers. Echion's niobium processing plant in Brazil. Photo: Courtesy Echion. EnPower CEO Adrian Yao told me that industrial robots such as those used in warehouses are a good market for smaller battery manufacturers because, at least for now, the robot market is too small for battery giants to want to target. “This is especially the case with a new chemistry that's not your typical flavor,” he said. The niobium batteries “are workhorses. You’re going to be able to use them for years and years and years,” said Jean de la Verpillière, CEO of Echion. --- Noteworthy China’s BYD installed its 10,000th ultrafast charging EV station in China last week. BYD, which calls the stations “lash chargers, has said it wants to install 20,000 of them in the country by the end of the year. The charges aim to charge up an EV in just 9 minutes. China’s XPeng claims it will eventually make higher profit margins on humanoid robots than it does on the sale of EVs. XPeng Co-President Brian Gu told The Wall Street Journal that Iron, the company’s current humanoid robot, could earn gross margins of more than 50%. title: „Infrastruktur(en)“ – ARL-Journal 01/2026 ist online verfügbar!
content:
„Infrastruktur(en)“ – ARL-Journal 01/2026 ist online verfügbar!
Infrastrukturen sind allgegenwärtig und doch bleiben sie im Alltag häufig unsichtbar. Sie fallen auf, wenn sie ausfallen, wenn z. B. der Strom wegbleibt, die Schule schließt, das Bahnnetz oder das Internet zusammenbricht. In Zeiten des Funktionierens hingegen sind sie das Selbstverständlichste der Welt: die unsichtbare Voraussetzung des gesellschaftlichen Alltags, das Rückgrat, auf dem Wirtschaft, Wohlstand und Zusammenleben ruhen. Gerade in dieser Unsichtbarkeit liegt eine politisch-planerische und wissenschaftliche Herausforderung: Infrastrukturen werden unterschätzt – in ihrer Fragilität, in ihrer Gestaltungsmacht, in ihrer Zukunftsbedeutung.
Das vorliegende Themenheft nimmt einige infrastrukturbezogene Herausforderungen in den Blick. Es versammelt Beiträge, die Infrastrukturen in ihrer Breite denken – nicht nur als technische Systeme, sondern als gesellschaftliche Verhältnisse, die den Raum strukturieren. Als Ausdruck politisch-planerischer Entscheidungen, als Bedingung sozialer Teilhabe und als Hebel der notwendigen sozial-ökologischen Transformation.
Timothy Moss richtet den Blick auf Berliner Infrastrukturgeschichte(n) und zeigt, wie sich Geschichte als Orientierungshilfe für gegenwärtige Herausforderungen und heutige Transformationsanforderungen nutzen lässt.
Cordula Kropp plädiert für einen Paradigmenwandel in der Infrastrukturpolitik und rückt Infrastrukturen als Hebel der sozial-ökologischen Transformation in den Fokus.
Angela Million und Janet Merkel illustrieren das Potenzial der Mehrfachnutzung von Infrastrukturen und zeigen, dass räumliche Planung und Gestaltung nicht nur die Verteilung von Infrastrukturen beeinflusst, sondern auch, ob, wie und von wem diese zeitlich genutzt werden können.
Karsten Zimmermann und Lena Unger blicken auf Rechenzentren als den materiellen Kern digitaler Infrastruktur und skizzieren erste international vergleichende Betrachtungen der Governance von Rechenzentren in sechs Staaten.
Angesichts der weltweit stark veränderten Sicherheitslagen befassen sich Axel Priebs und Andreas Klee mit Fragen der Verteidigung und dem Bevölkerungsschutz. Resiliente Infrastrukturen sind dabei kein Selbstzweck, sondern die Voraussetzung für die Handlungsfähigkeit des Staates in Krisenzeiten.
Elke Dahlbeck und Stefan Gärtner fragen, wie Infrastrukturinvestitionen angesichts wachsender kommunaler Verschuldung gesichert werden können. Das ist besonders bedeutsam, da sich gerade auf kommunaler Ebene die Lebensqualität und die Sicherung von Teilhabe entscheiden.
Jana Liebe und Christoph Frenkel stellen am Beispiel der Thüringer Industrie dar, wie die Dekarbonisierung der Energieversorgung gelingen kann. Sie bündeln Erkenntnisse aus sieben Jahren angewandter Energieforschung.

Projektstart »DatMuSSS«: KI soll Qualitätsbewertung und Sortierung von Rundholz in Sägewerken automatisieren

In ersten Machbarkeitsstudien wurden akustische Signale von Holz erfasst. DatMuSSS entwickelt daraus ein nachrüstbares Messsystem für Sägewerke.

Fraunhofer IDMT

Thüringer Forschungsprojekt will ein kostengünstiges, nachrüstbares Prüfsystem für Sägewerke entwickeln
Mit dem Start des Forschungsprojekts DatMuSSS – Datengetriebene Multimodale Sortierung von Stammholz im Sägewerk wollen das Fraunhofer-Institut für Digitale Medientechnologie IDMT, die Technische Universität Ilmenau, die Unternehmen Vision & Control und PREMETEC Automation sowie das Sägewerk Schwarzmühle die automatisierte Holzsortierung voranbringen. Gemeinsam erforschen die Thüringer Partner, wie sich die Qualität von Rundholz mithilfe künstlicher Intelligenz zuverlässig bewerten und daraus automatisiert die passende Sortierung ableiten lässt.
Ziel des Forschungsprojekts soll die Entwicklung eines kostengünstigen und nachrüstbaren Prüfsystems sein, das vor allem kleinen und mittleren Sägewerken eine wirtschaftliche Automatisierung der Sortierprozesse ermöglichen soll.
Wenn ein Holzlieferung im Sägewerk eintrifft, entscheidet die korrekte Bewertung jeden einzelnen Stamms über dessen Qualitätseinstufung und somit über seinen späteren Verkaufspreis und seine Verwendung.
Bis heute erfolgt die Begutachtung der Qualität insbesondere in kleinen und mittleren Sägewerken häufig durch erfahrene Fachkräfte mittels Sichtkontrolle. Innere Schäden wie Hohlräume oder Fäule bleiben dabei jedoch oft verborgen. Gleichzeitig erschweren Fachkräftemangel und steigender Kostendruck die zuverlässige Qualitätskontrolle. Genau hier setzt das neue Forschungsvorhaben DatMuSSS an.
+++ Wie kann ein Baumstamm innerhalb weniger Sekunden zuverlässig bewertet werden? +++
Im Projekt werden erstmals akustische, geometrische und bildliche Informationen von Holzstämmen gemeinsam ausgewertet. Kameras erfassen die Stirnseiten und Mantelflächen der Stämme, akustische Messungen liefern zusätzliche Hinweise auf die innere Holzstruktur und Laserscanner werten Informationen zu Größe und Form aus.
Aus diesen Daten lernt eine KI, die Holzqualität automatisch zu bewerten und daraus die Grundlage für eine automatisierte Sortierung abzuleiten.
Es soll eine robuste Lösung entstehen, die unter realen Produktionsbedingungen arbeitet und einfach in den laufenden Betrieb integriert werden kann.
+++ Thüringer Partner entwickeln Lösung gemeinsam vor Ort +++
Das Forschungsprojekt DatMuSSS verbindet regionale Partner aus Forschung, Technologieentwicklung und Industrie, um gemeinsam eine praxistaugliche Lösung für die automatisierte Holzsortierung zu entwickeln.
Das Fraunhofer-Institut für Digitale Medientechnologie IDMT leitet das Forschungsprojekt und bringt seine Expertise in der KI-basierten Analyse und Auswertung akustischer Signale für Industrieanwendungen ein. Im Projekt entwickelt das Institut Verfahren, mit denen die erfassten Messdaten verknüpft und zur automatischen Bewertung der Holzqualität genutzt werden.
Das Fachgebiet Qualitätssicherung und Industrielle Bildverarbeitung der Technischen Universität Ilmenau entwickelt optische Verfahren und KI-Methoden zur Erfassung und Auswertung sichtbarer Holzmerkmale.
Die Vision & Control GmbH unterstützt das Vorhaben mit ihrer langjährigen Erfahrung in der industriellen Bildverarbeitung und bei der Auswahl der passenden Kamerasysteme für die Erfassung der Bilddaten.
Die PREMETEC Automation GmbH entwickelt eine automatisierte Einheit mit der gezielt die Holzstämme in Schwingungen versetzt und so akustisch vermessen werden können. Das Unternehmen kümmert sich außerdem um die Integration dieser akustischen Prüfeinheit in bestehende Sägewerksanlagen und -prozesse.
Das Sägewerk Schwarzmühle stellt als Anwendungspartner die Testumgebung und die akustischen und optischen Daten für Entwicklung und Validierung des Prüfsystems bereit. Außerdem bringt das Unternehmen sein Wissen zur Bewertung von Rundholz ein und unterstützt damit die Zuordnung der automatisch erfassten Daten zu den tatsächlichen Holzqualitäten.
»Die regionale Nähe aller Projektpartner ist ein großer Vorteil für das Projekt. Sie ermöglicht uns, die entwickelten akustischen und optischen Sensoren, KI-Modelle und Automatisierungslösungen schnell unter realen Bedingungen im Sägewerk zu erproben und gemeinsam weiterzuentwickeln. Gleichzeitig können wir die Integration in bestehende Anlagen und laufende Betriebsprozesse direkt vor Ort testen und frühzeitig prüfen, wie sich die Lösung wirtschaftlich und zuverlässig in der Praxis umsetzen lässt«, erklärt Projektleiter Florian Klein vom Fraunhofer IDMT.
+++ Ziel: Entwicklung einer kostengünstigen und nachrüstbaren Alternative zu aufwändigen Prüfsystemen +++
Für die Bewertung von Rundholz kommen aktuell häufig Röntgen- oder Computertomographie-Systeme zum Einsatz. Diese CT-Systeme ermöglichen detaillierte Einblicke in den Stammaufbau, sind jedoch teuer, benötigen viel Platz und lassen sich im laufenden platzintensiv und rechnen sich für viele Sägewerke Betrieb kaum.
DatMuSSS verfolgt deshalb bewusst einen anderen Ansatz: Es wird ein einfach nachrüstbares Prüfsystem für bestehende Sägewerksanlagen entwickelt. Unternehmen sollen die Technologie ohne grundlegende Umbauten in ihre vorhandenen Prozesse integrieren können. Eine vergleichbare Kombination aus akustischer und visueller Sensorik für die automatisierte Holzsortierung ist derzeit am Markt nicht verfügbar.
»Wir wollen vor allem kleine und mittlere Betriebe dabei unterstützen, die Holzqualität künftig schneller, objektiver und wirtschaftlicher zu bewerten. Mit der KI-basierten automatischen Holzbewertung wollen wir dafür eine wichtige Grundlage schaffen. Bereits jetzt erreichen uns Nachfragen von Sägewerken und holzverarbeitenden Unternehmen aus anderen Regionen Deutschlands. Das zeigt uns, dass der Bedarf unseres Ansatzes weit über Thüringen hinausgeht«, freut sich Florian Klein.
+++ Förderung und Projektlaufzeit +++
Das Verbundprojekt »DatMuSSS – Datengetriebene Multimodale Sortierung von Stammholz im Sägewerk« wird vom Bundesministerium für Forschung, Technologie und Raumfahrt (BMFTR) im Rahmen des Programms »WIR! – Wandel durch Innovation in der Region« im Bündnis Holz-21-regio unter dem Kennzeichen 03WIR3620A gefördert. Das Vorhaben läuft von August 2026 bis Januar 2028.

title: Investments in co-located solar-plus-storage reach $25 billion in H1, says BloombergNEF - Energy Storage
content: Global investment in renewable energy reached $327.5 billion (€281 billion) in the first half of 2026, virtually unchanged from the previous six months but 21% below the record set in the second half of 2024. Data from BloombergNEF (BNEF) show that renewable energy deployment remains on track despite regulatory changes in key markets, including the United States and China. Investment, however, is increasingly shifting toward assets that offer greater flexibility in managing revenues. Storage drives hybrid projects Financing for standalone utility-scale solar fell more sharply than investment in onshore wind. Investment in standalone solar PV declined 20% year on year to $75.4 billion (€64.7 billion), its lowest level since the solar investment boom began in 2021. Growing revenue uncertainty, driven by solar price cannibalization, curtailment and grid congestion, is pushing investors and developers toward more flexible project configurations. Against this backdrop, co-located solar-plus-storage projects attracted a record $25 billion (€21.5 billion) in investment in the first half of 2026. The figure was nearly double the total recorded in the second half of 2025 and three times the amount invested in the first half of that year. The United States and Australia led investment in the segment. US accelerates ahead of incentive expiration The United States was the second-largest market for renewable energy investment, behind China but ahead of the European Union, recording 54% year-on-year growth. Developers accelerated project financing to meet tax credit deadlines and respond to surging electricity demand, driven in part by data centers. Solar investment rose 41% to a record $45.8 billion (€39.3 billion), while wind investment reached $13.8 billion, more than double the previous year’s figure. Projects that remain eligible for tax credits could sustain construction activity in the short term, with the final installations scheduled through 2030. BloombergNEF expects new renewable energy installations in 2026 to fall below 2025 levels, marking the first year-on-year decline in more than a decade. It expects growth to resume in 2027. title: Grenergy plans 516.9 MWp solar plant with 3.01 GWh BESS in Chile - Energy Storage
content: Solar Antofagasta has submitted the environmental impact declaration for the Parque Fotovoltaico Antofagasta 1 project to Chile’s Environmental Impact Assessment System (SEIA). The project, whose parent group is identified in the documentation as Grenergy Renovables, comprises a 516.92 MWp solar plant and a 430 MW/approximately 3,010 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS), equivalent to seven hours of storage. The project will be located in the María Elena municipality, Tocopilla province, in the Antofagasta region, covering a total area of 834.58 hectares. Permanent and temporary works will occupy 402.37 hectares, with the remainder left free of installations. The solar plant will comprise 820,512 modules rated at 630 W each. Electricity generated by the plant can be stored in the BESS for subsequent injection into Chile’s National Electricity System (SEN), shifting energy delivery toward periods of higher demand. For grid connection, the project includes the new Salitre step-up substation, rated at 33/220 kV, and a 20.7 km high-voltage transmission line. The line will comprise 59 structures – two line gantries and 57 lattice towers – and connect to the existing 220 kV Kimal substation, which is owned by a third party. The environmental impact declaration estimates investment of approximately $250 million for the solar plant, including the transmission line and substation, and a further $270 million for the BESS. This brings the investment described in the executive summary to about $520 million. The figure differs from the $593 million attributed to the project in reports published after its submission to SEIA; the attached document explicitly breaks down the two lower amounts. Construction is expected to take 20 months and require up to 400 workers, with an average workforce of 200. The documents schedule construction to begin in May 2028, subject to a favorable Environmental Qualification Resolution (RCA) and the required sectoral permits. Grid connection and commercial operation are scheduled for February 2030. The plant is expected to operate for 40 years, through February 2070, while decommissioning will take 18 months. Average staffing during operations is expected to be five people, rising to a maximum of nine during maintenance activities. The voluntary environmental commitments included in the filing include a coordination plan with the Tocopilla provincial fire department covering procedures for potential battery fires or explosions. The document also outlines specific measures for BESS fires, chemical explosions involving battery racks, and potential incidents during the transportation, installation, or storage of lithium batteries. title: Shell sells Sonnen to Tiven - pv magazine Global
content:
Nearly three years have passed since Shell announced that it intended to divest its wholly owned subsidiary Sonnen and was seeking a new investor or at least a majority shareholder. The sale has now been completed. The companies involved did not issue any official announcements, although German business newspaper
Handelsblatt
learned of the transaction and reported on it around two weeks ago.
In response to an inquiry from
pv magazine
, Shell confirmed that it completed the sale of Sonnen to Tiven. “This step supports our ongoing efforts to optimize our portfolio. We believe Tiven and Aurelius Water Rise are well positioned to support Sonnen’s further development,” a Shell spokesperson said.
Tiven is an international asset manager and family office. It has an office in Munich, although
pv magazine
was unable to reach it by phone at the number provided. An email inquiry from
pv magazine
also went unanswered at the time of publication.
Gert Purkert is a key figure at Tiven, according to
Handelsblatt
. He is managing director of Tiven, founded Aurelius and is a former McKinsey consultant.
Sonnen did not initially respond to a request for comment.
Handelsblatt
reported that Tiven intends to restructure Sonnen with the aim of preparing it for a future resale. The newspaper was unable to obtain further details. Citing people familiar with the matter, it said the purchase price was in the low hundreds of millions of euros.
Shell acquired Sonnen in 2019 for nearly €500 million. Given the residential battery storage provider’s weak financial performance in recent years and an additional capital injection in 2024 to maintain its operations,
Handelsblatt
described the investment as a deal that had cost Shell losses totaling around €1 billion.
At this year’s The smarter E Europe trade fair in Munich, Sonnen did not have its own booth and was instead represented by a “Coffee Corner.” Shortly before the event, Sonnen Chief Revenue Officer Andreas Plenk told
pv magazine
that the decision reflected a change in the company’s sales and marketing strategy in Germany.
Asked about the company’s business performance, Plenk said: “In 2025, we returned to growth despite an overall declining market, and our order books are already well filled this year. In general, demand is slowly picking up again after two weaker years. At the same time, many installers remain hesitant to expand their capacity. This is often due to uncertainty over whether the upward trend will continue. Our approach offers them added value during this uncertain phase. We are trading some visibility at the trade fair for better service and closer cooperation with our partners.”
How that strategy will evolve under the new ownership remains to be seen. At present, however, there is no publicly available information about Tiven’s specific plans for Sonnen.

title: ClearVue announces coating breakthrough for energy-generating solar glass - pv magazine Global
content:
Australian building-integrated PV (BIPV) specialist ClearVue Technologies has announced a manufacturing breakthrough that allows its energy-generating Gen 3 glass units to accept high-performance soft low-emissivity (Low-E) coatings using the same established systems as conventional commercial glazing.
Perth-headquartered ClearVue’s
Gen3 solar vision glass
product features PV cells integrated into a laminated glass unit designed to generate electricity while maintaining glass transparency. The company said its units can generate more than 50 W of energy per square metre while maintaining up to 80% visible light transmittance.
In a boost to the commercial opportunities for the technology, ClearVue said its glass units can now be coated via a “magnetron sputter-coating process” after the PV cells have been laminated and processed, allowing a Low-E coating to be applied to the finished solar glass units. These coatings help control the amount of solar heat entering a building and are commonly specified across commercial façade projects worldwide.
“This removes a practical barrier for the industry,” ClearVue Chief Executive Officer Doug Hunt said. “It means energy-generating glass can be considered alongside conventional façade products, rather than requiring an entirely separate design or manufacturing process.”
“This is an important step in moving energy-generating façades from a specialist product towards standard commercial practice.”
According to ClearVue, the manufacturing capability allows the coating to be applied on surface 4, the room-facing side of the double-glazed unit, where it provides the greatest reduction in solar heat gain.
ClearVue believes it is currently the only BIPV supplier able to offer this capability while also generating renewable energy from the same glazing unit. The company said other BIPV products typically apply the coating on surface 5 of a triple-glazed unit, where thermal performance is reduced.
Hunt said the manufacturing breakthrough makes it easier for the façade industry to adopt energy-generating glazing without changing the way projects are already designed and delivered.
“For energy-generating glass to become widely used, it needs to fit within the systems the industry already understands and trusts,” he said.
“Architects and engineers can continue specifying the performance they need, while glass processors can use their existing production infrastructure. The difference is that the glass can now also generate clean energy for the building.”
ClearVue said it validated the new capability at glass manufacturer AGC Interpane’s facility in Germany, where the Gen 3 Vision Glass units were cleaned, coated and tested using the same production line and settings as conventional float glass, with no changes required to the coating process.
The manufacturing development is part of a series of recent commercial and technical milestones for ClearVue, including securing major
international certifications
for its Gen 3 Solar Vision Glass and its
thermal management junction box
The company’s ClearVue-Helios
rooftop solar panel
has also recently been added to the Clean Energy Council’s approved products list, ensuring it can connect to the grid and is eligible for all government grant and subsidy programs.

title: Mitsui E&S commercializes marine ammonia engine
content:
Mitsui E&S commercializes marine ammonia engine
Two-stroke, dual-fuel engines and fuel supply systems now available to customers
Japan-based Mitsui E&S has completed the commercialization phase of its two-stroke, ammonia-fueled marine engines and ammonia fuel supply systems (AFSS), now able to serve customers with both products from its Tamano manufacturing base. Having now established a full “supply framework for marine propulsion systems”, Mitsui E&S is focused on the “practical implementation” of ammonia-fueled vessels.
Mitsui E&S has been pursuing a Japan-based engine manufacturing setup based on the Everllence B&W ME-LGIA model, with the technology licensed to Mitsui E&S by Denmark-based Everllence (formerly MAN ES). The initial prototypes of the “MITSUI-Everellence B&W 7S60ME-C10.5-LGIA-HPSCR” engine went through technical testing in Tamano in early 2025. This February, Mitsui E&S conducted tests of the integrated operation of the engine and the AFSS, witnessed by class society ClassNK. This recently-completed onshore testing has confirmed compliance of the integrated engine-AFSS setup with International Maritime Organization (IMO) NOX emissions limits: a key regulatory and environmental threshold for ammonia-fueled marine engines. Mitsui E&S plans to expand its capabilities to produce AFSS integrated systems compatible with WinGD’s ammonia-fueled X-DF-A engine, and Tamano may potentially be a future manufacturing site for a WinGD-licensed engine model.
On the vessel front, Mitsui E&S is part of two long-standing partnerships to deploy marine ammonia engines:
- Mitsui O.S.K. Lines, Namura Shipbuilding and Mitsubishi Shipbuilding’s large-size ammonia-powered ammonia carrier (under development since 2021), will use an Everllence two-stroke engine built by Mitsui E&S.
- And (from Singapore Maritime Week 2024) K Line, ITOCHU, Nihon Shipyard, MAN Energy Solutions (MAN ES), and Mitsui E&S agreed to develop and build 200,000 dwt Newcastlemax-size bulk carriers at Nihon Shipyard, equipped with ammonia-fueled engines built by Mitsui E&S in Japan.
The development of the AFSS utilized funds from the “Integrated Project for the Development and Social Implementation of Ammonia-Fueled Ships” scheme administered by Japan’s New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO). Expansion of the AFSS for onshore testing will be in part funded by the “Project to Promote the Construction of Zero-Emission Ships,” a joint initiative of the Ministry of the Environment and the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism.

title: Construction begins on Blue Point project
content:
Construction begins on Blue Point project
Project partners CF Industries, JERA, and Mitsui & Co. have broken ground on construction of Blue Point: a 1.4 million tons per year ammonia production facility fed with CCS-based hydrogen feedstock. The plant is located in Modeste, Louisiana, and is expected to begin low-carbon ammonia production in 2029.
Last June, Linde announced it would invest more than $400 million in a new on-site air-separation unit to supply oxygen and nitrogen to the plant. Topsoe’s SynCOR™ Ammonia production technology will be deployed at Blue Point. An autothermal reforming (ATR) ammonia production facility coupled with an onsite CO2 dehydration and compression unit, preparing emissions for transportation and eventual sequestration. CCS specialists 1PointFive and Enbridge will transport and sequester approximately 2.3 million tons of CO2 from Blue Point annually (~98% of the CO2 emissions generated in ammonia production) at its onshore Pelican Sequestration Hub in Louisiana. 1PointFive has already taken FID on the Pelican Hub, and the Class VI site is moving through the state-based approvals process. Electricity utility Entergy Louisiana will provide power for the site. CF Industries is investing an additional $550 million in scalable infrastructure (including product storage and loading) at the site, and will also be responsible for the operation and maintenance of the ammonia production facility. The site also includes room for future ammonia production expansion.
$3.7 billion has been invested by the Blue Point One joint venture members, with contributions allocated according to ownership levels. CF Industries holds 40% ownership, JERA 35% ownership, and Mitsui 25% ownership.
We are proud to break ground on the Blue Point One joint venture, a transformative project that brings together American energy resources, world-class engineering and partnerships, and trusted global allies. Most importantly, this facility will serve people, growing access to the reliable, domestic nitrogen supply American farmers need to feed the world, expanding our nation’s export capacity through shipping American-made energy to global markets and creating jobs in Louisiana.
CF Industries President and Chief Executive Officer Chris Bohn, in his organisation’s official press release, 26 Aug 2026
Today’s groundbreaking marks an important milestone for Blue Point One and brings us one step closer to establishing a reliable low-carbon ammonia value chain. At JERA, we believe that energy transition must be supported by practical projects and strong partnerships across the value chain. Blue Point One reflects this belief, bringing together partners with a shared commitment to build the foundation needed to scale lower-carbon ammonia for the future.
JERA Global Energy Solutions Chief Executive Officer, JERA Senior Managing Executive Officer, Chief Operating Officer of Low Carbon Fuels Business Irtiza Sayyed, in CF Industries’ official press release, 26 Aug 2026
We are delighted to celebrate the groundbreaking of Blue Point One and sincerely thank our partners, the State of Louisiana, the local community, and all stakeholders whose support has made this milestone possible. Building on Mitsui’s long-term commitment to Louisiana, this project further strengthens the enduring partnership between the United States and Japan and advances a low-carbon ammonia value chain that contributes to supply chain resilience in the U.S., Japan, and beyond. We look forward to working closely with our partners to deliver this project safely and successfully, while contributing to the long-term prosperity of the region and its communities.
Mitsui & Co., Ltd President and Chief Executive Officer Kenichi Hori, in CF Industries’ official press release, 26 Aug 2026

title: AFRY wins Uniper FEED for NorthStarH2 e-methanol plant
content:
NorthStarH2 is planned to produce around 115,000 tonnes of e-methanol per year. The plant will combine green hydrogen produced through electrolysis, powered by 175 MW of renewable electricity, with biogenic CO₂ captured from Jämtkraft’s biomass-fired heat and power plant in Lugnvik, Sweden.
AFRY’s front-end engineering design (FEED) scope covers process design, plant engineering, operating philosophy, technical specifications, health, safety, and environment in design, and coordination with original equipment manufacturers supplying electrolysis, carbon capture, and methanol synthesis technologies. The FEED work is intended to advance NorthStarH2 from early project development toward a final investment decision.
The assignment started in late August 2026 and is expected to run until summer 2027. Uniper plans to make its final investment decision for NorthStarH2 in 2028, with commissioning currently scheduled for 2031. Uniper is developing NorthStarH2 through Sydkraft Hydrogen AB, in cooperation with Jämtkraft.
“E-methanol will play an increasingly important role in decarbonizing hard-to-abate sectors such as transport and chemicals. AFRY is honored to support Uniper in transforming this vision into a technically robust and investment-ready project,” said Guy Skantze, Head of Chemicals and Biorefining at AFRY.
Broghan Helgeson, NorthStarH2’s project manager at Uniper, said: “NorthStarH2 is an important project in Uniper’s energy transition portfolio, and we are pleased that the FEED contract with AFRY is now in place. We look forward to continuing our successful collaboration and completing the FEED phase together.”

title: Ballard acquires GeoPura in £275m hydrogen deal | Hydrogen Tech World.com
content:
Founded in 2019, GeoPura designs, manufactures, and operates its Hydrogen Power Unit (HPU) systems, which use Ballard fuel cell modules to convert hydrogen into clean electricity for off-grid applications. The company also produces green hydrogen via electrolysis at dedicated production facilities and operates what it describes as the UK’s largest compressed hydrogen distribution fleet.
The combined business brings together GeoPura’s HPU platform, hydrogen fuel production, and logistics with Ballard’s fuel cell technology to create a turnkey Energy-as-a-Service (EaaS) offering. Ballard said the end-to-end capability strengthens its market presence across Europe and opens commercial opportunities in North America.
The transaction includes total upfront consideration of £275.0 million, comprising £82.5 million in cash, 49,584,212 newly issued Ballard common shares, and restricted share units to be settled in 12 months for an additional 1,084,540 common shares. Former GeoPura shareholders hold approximately 14.1% of Ballard’s outstanding common shares on a pro-forma basis. Ballard may pay up to £27.5 million in additional contingent consideration subject to specified post-closing financial milestones.
“Today marks a pivotal milestone in Ballard’s evolution as we officially welcome GeoPura to our organization,” said Marty Neese, Chief Executive Officer of Ballard. “By bringing GeoPura’s clean power generation platform together with Ballard’s fuel cell stack engineering under one roof, we provide our customers with a single, integrated source for reliable zero-emission power.”
Andrew Cunningham, who has assumed the role of President of Ballard, added: “Uniting with Ballard creates a stronger, more resilient partner for customers facing increasingly complex energy challenges. Together, we combine world-leading fuel cell technology with proven hydrogen power production and infrastructure expertise to deliver reliable, zero-emission energy where and when it’s needed.”

title: 台湾拟将小型模块化反应堆和核聚变纳入新能源探索
content:
台湾拟将小型模块化反应堆和核聚变纳入新能源探索
卓荣泰当天出席新能源论坛时表示，对台湾而言，尚未进入大规模商业应用、或研发技术仍未成熟的能源类型，均可视为新能源探索对象。除地热、小水力、氢能等技术外，新型核能也被列为未来持续观察和研究的方向。
在SMR方面，卓荣泰称，台湾方面此前已表明愿意开放讨论各类技术，并编列部分预算，希望与国际先进技术接轨。当前全球SMR技术路线较为多元，主要包括轻水堆、高温气冷堆等设计。美国X-energy公司(X-energy)开发的Xe-100采用高温气冷堆方案;通用电气维尔诺瓦日立核能公司(GE Vernova Hitachi Nuclear Energy)推进的BWRX-300延续沸水堆技术，加拿大安大略省达灵顿项目已进入建设阶段;西屋电气公司(Westinghouse)的AP300则采用压水堆技术，以AP1000设计为基础缩小规模，单机发电容量约300兆瓦。
除SMR外，台湾也开始建立自主核聚变研究能力。台湾科技主管部门自2023年起支持“磁约束高温等离子体研究”整合型计划，由台湾相关研究机构与高校合作，建设首座自主研发的小型球形托卡马克研究装置FIRST。该计划目前进入第二阶段，预计2026年完成系统整合，2027年启动运行测试，研究重点包括磁场稳定控制等离子体以及延长等离子体约束时间。
全球核聚变技术也在推进商业化验证。国际热核聚变实验堆(ITER)是目前全球规模最大的托卡马克核聚变实验项目，目标是整合未来核聚变电厂所需关键技术。美国联邦聚变系统公司(Commonwealth Fusion Systems，CFS)正在马萨诸塞州建设SPARC高磁场托卡马克装置，目标是在2030年代初期提供约400兆瓦电力。
对于既有核电机组是否重新启动，卓荣泰表示，核三厂目前正依程序进行相关评估。台电需提出再运行计划和自主安全检查，并经核安全监管机构审定，同时评估设备更新及新技术导入的可行性，以确认核三厂是否具备重新启动条件。
卓荣泰表示，台湾方面面对核电仍维持“核安无虞、核废有解、社会有共识”三项原则。在既有电力建设规划下，将持续跟踪SMR、核聚变等新型核能技术发展，为未来能源选项预作准备。

title: 玛努尔核电产出国产重量最大细长抽锭电渣锭
content:
玛努尔核电产出国产重量最大细长抽锭电渣锭
2026年8月30日，烟台台海玛努尔核电设备有限公司150吨级气氛保护电渣炉60t抽锭工位成功产出直径约1270㎜、重量61.2吨的细长电渣钢锭，刷新国产特种冶金装备制造纪录，为核电高端锻件供应夯实装备基础。
本次生产的61.2吨细长抽锭电渣钢锭，钢锭外观成型规整，表面质量优良。冶炼过程中，气氛保护、熔速控制、液面精准控制、全自动交换及抽锭全流程等设备和运行稳定可控。该钢锭为目前国内重量最大的细长型抽锭电渣锭，代表国产大吨位抽锭电渣装备实现又一次关键性跨越，为核电高端锻件供应夯实装备基础。
相较于传统冶炼工位，60t抽锭工位可按需定制细长型电渣钢锭，钢锭的尺寸、重量能够精准适配各类核电锻件用锭的工况需求，显著提升钢锭综合利用率。助力推动特种冶金向着精益化、大型化、高效化方向发展。
作为核电高端装备核心配套制造单元，150吨级气氛保护电渣炉60t抽锭工位连续取得生产突破，补齐国内超大吨位细长抽锭电渣锭的制造短板，摆脱部分高端核电锻件用锭的供给制约，为百万千瓦级核电站一回路主管道等关键核电装备国产化提供坚实材料保障，助力我国核电产业链自主可控能力持续提升。

title: 诺瓦聚变完成12亿元Pre-A系列融资
content:
2026-08-31 09:50 来源：诺瓦聚变
诺瓦聚变能源科技(上海)有限公司近日宣布完成总额12亿元Pre-A系列融资，包含Pre-A轮和Pre-A+轮。公司称，自成立以来16个月内，已先后完成5亿元天使轮、7亿元天使+轮和本轮融资，累计融资规模达24亿元，投后估值超过100亿元。
本轮融资中，美团龙珠、高瓴创投继续参与，联想创投、国中资本作为新战略投资方加入。公司表示，本轮资金将主要用于新装置建设、关键技术迭代、产业化基地筹备以及后续聚变能输出验证等工作。
诺瓦聚变聚焦场反位形(FRC)小型模块化、分布式聚变小堆(FRC-SMR)研发与产业化。按照公司披露的技术路线，该方案拟通过高β值等离子体约束、强磁场与模块化工程设计实现装置小型化，单堆功率目标为50MW，面向AI数据中心等高密度、连续低碳用能场景提供分布式能源解决方案。
公司创始人郭后扬长期从事聚变等离子体研究，曾参与托卡马克和FRC相关实验研究工作。诺瓦聚变称，目前公司已形成覆盖FRC-SMR核心技术链条的研发团队，并在高功率全固态开关、模块化强磁场磁体、大型石英真空腔体国产化制造、纳秒级精密控制采集系统等方向完成工程样机实测验证，相关技术专利已申请。
据介绍，诺瓦聚变首套装置“诺瓦一号”已完成工程设计和核心部件研制，进入总装集成阶段。其关键部件包括石英真空室、模块化磁体、大功率全固态脉冲电源及纳秒级控制采集系统等，真空抽气、诊断、加料等辅助系统也已定型，土建基础已完工。
按照规划，诺瓦聚变计划在2026年底实现“诺瓦一号”首次等离子体放电，目标是在2029年开展氘氚等效聚变净能量增益Q>1验证，并在2030年代前半叶建设50MW至100MW级商用示范电站。公司还表示，正与地方政府推进FRC-SMR聚变小堆产业化基地的前期筹备、选址和规划，范围涵盖聚变小堆、实验电站、研发中心及关键部件制造等环节。

title: 广西白龙核电1号机组核岛CA01模块顺利吊装就位
content:
2026-08-31 08:39 来源：国家电投
8月29日，国家电投集团广西核电白龙核电1号机组核岛CA01模块精准就位，标志着核岛施工进入土建与安装并行推进新阶段。
▲8月29日，国家电投集团广西白龙核电1号机组核岛CA01模块吊装作业正在有序进行。
CA01模块就位于核岛反应堆厂房，是反应堆压力容器、蒸发器、稳压器等主设备的安装房间。模块整体呈T字形，外形尺寸长28米、宽29米、高24米，由47个子模块组成，起吊总重量约1167吨，是该核岛最大、最重的结构模块。本次吊装于8时07分开始起吊，经过起钩、悬停、回转、下落、调整等系列动作，于12时58分顺利就位，整个过程安全可控，平稳有序。
▲8月29日，国家电投集团广西白龙核电1号机组核岛CA01模块吊装作业正在有序进行。
为保障本次吊装作业安全有序实施，国家电投集团广西核电充分总结前期CA20、CA05等模块吊装经验，从严把控各项先决条件，实行清单化管理，逐项压实责任、闭环落实。在技术层面，项目团队开展吊装全过程仿真计算，对模块采取防变形加固措施;结合模块尺寸参数，对核岛安装区域进行精准测量与三维扫描，提前识别并消除干涉物项;严格核对模块重量，实时更新重心计算数据，顺利完成模块调平，实现模块吊装精准就位。
广西白龙核电项目厂址位于广西防城港市江山半岛的最南端，是国家电投集团在桂开发的首座核电站，也是广西建设国家综合能源安全保障区的标志性工程。项目规划建设2台CAP1000核电机组和4台“国和一号”机组，总装机约850万千瓦，一次规划、分期实施。一期工程1号机组已于2025年12月实现FCD(浇筑核岛第一罐混凝土)，目前处于建设安装阶段。

title: 中广核与中船集团深化核电及新能源领域合作
content:
2026-08-31 13:52 来源：中广核
8月28日，中国广核集团有限公司党委副书记、总经理庞松涛在中广核大厦会见中国船舶集团有限公司(简称“中船集团”)党组书记、董事长徐鹏一行，双方围绕核电、新能源、工业软件、科技创新等领域合作开展深入交流。中船集团党组成员、副总经理彭原璞，总经理助理马云翔，集团公司党委常委、副总经理蔡振，集团公司党委委员、中广核电力副总裁、总法律顾问周建平参加会谈。
庞松涛对徐鹏一行的到访表示热烈欢迎。他指出，中广核与中船集团的合作始于大亚湾核电站，至今已走过四十余年历程，合作领域从核电逐步拓展到环境治理、新能源开发、工业软件等多个方面，并在核电应急柴油机、风电装备等领域取得了丰硕成果。面向“十五五”，他希望双方在巩固现有合作基础的同时，进一步拓展装备制造、科技创新等新领域的合作，更好服务国家战略大局。
徐鹏对中广核长期以来给予的支持表示衷心感谢。他指出，中广核是中船集团重要的战略合作伙伴，双方互补性强、业务契合度高，具有广阔合作空间。中船集团将立足主责主业，进一步发挥产业链协同优势，建立完善常态化对接沟通机制，持续深化跨行业开放协作与务实交流，共同谋划推进重大项目落实落地，携手开创产业协同高质量发展新格局。
中船集团综合管理部、战略规划部，中船科技、中船海舟、第七一九研究所、中船动力相关负责人;集团公司董事会秘书、战略规划部总经理方春法，集团公司综合管理部、科技数字化部以及中广核工程、中广核研究院、中广核新能源、中广核数科等单位相关负责人参加会谈。

title: 扎波罗热核电站依靠应急柴油发电维持运行
content:
扎波罗热核电站依靠应急柴油发电维持运行
国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 近日表示，扎波罗热核电站 (ZNPP) 外部电力供应中断后，已连续一周以上依靠应急柴油发电机维持关键安全系统运行。该机构现场专家组检查后确认，截至当地时间23日，电站柴油储备约可支撑10天，已接近最低监管要求。
据国际原子能机构介绍，扎波罗热核电站自20日起失去与仅存330千伏佩罗斯普拉夫纳-1号外部输电线路的连接。此后，电站启用多台应急柴油发电机，为六台反应堆以及乏燃料冷却和储存相关水泵等关键设备供电。
国际原子能机构总干事拉斐尔·格罗西 (Rafael Grossi) 表示，确保核电站拥有充足柴油燃料至关重要。若外部电力近期无法恢复，且额外柴油燃料不能及时运抵，电站可能在约10天后面临更严峻的供电风险。
燃料补给方面，国际原子能机构称，扎波罗热核电站外部燃料库上一次接收燃料是在去年3月，原计划于5月进行的后续补给因运输安排延误而未能按期完成。自2025年3月以来，出于安全原因，国际原子能机构现场专家组也未能进入相关燃料储存设施开展核查。
除供电问题外，电站周边安全形势仍影响核安全保障工作。国际原子能机构现场专家组报告称，近期电站附近多次出现爆炸声。本周，扎波罗热核电站厂区内还发生三起无人机相关事件，其中一起发生在冷却池附近并造成两名电站员工受伤，另一起发生在干式乏燃料储存设施附近。另有报告称，一架无人机撞击了电站机组喷淋系统。电站辐射水平目前仍处于正常范围。
国际原子能机构表示，正在就恢复外部输电线路所需的现场安全安排继续沟通，并推进对乌克兰核设施的支持计划。相关计划包括向切尔诺贝利核电站运送便携式发电设备，并向乌克兰核监管机构提供剂量计、电池和逆变器等设备。

title: 匈牙利拟为保克什二期核电站追加约3亿欧元资金
content:
匈牙利拟为保克什二期核电站追加约3亿欧元资金
匈牙利政府拟为保克什二期核电站项目追加1116亿福林资金，折合约3.055亿欧元。相关款项已被纳入2026年预算修正案草案，预计将提交匈牙利议会审议。
根据预算文件，保克什二期项目在2026年底前获得的财政支持将由950亿福林增至2066亿福林，约合5.655亿欧元。按相关测算，过去12年间，匈牙利政府已直接向该项目拨款6287亿福林，超过17亿欧元;若计入本次预算安排，累计财政支持将超过22亿欧元。
保克什二期核电站由俄罗斯国家原子能公司 (Rosatom) 参与设计和建设。Rosatom方面此前表示，项目施工正按照计划以及匈牙利承包商批准的进度推进。今年2月5日，5号机组浇筑第一罐混凝土。按照国际原子能机构 (IAEA) 标准，该项目由此正式进入核电站在建阶段，标志着工程从前期准备转入主体建设。
保克什二期核电站建设依据俄匈两国2014年签署的政府间协议，以及两台VVER-1200机组建设相关基础合同推进。该项目预计总投资125亿欧元，最初计划约80%资金来自俄罗斯贷款。新机组计划于2030年代初投入运行。
目前运行中的保克什核电站位于布达佩斯以南约100公里的多瑙河畔，建于20世纪80年代，配备4台VVER-440反应堆。该电站承担匈牙利约45%的发电量和36%的电力消费需求。保克什二期投运后，保克什核电站总装机容量预计将由目前的2000兆瓦提高至4400兆瓦。

title: 日本拟将茨城县常陆大宫市纳入核废料处置选址调查
content:
日本拟将茨城县常陆大宫市纳入核废料处置选址调查
据知情人士8月31日透露，日本经济产业省正考虑在茨城县常陆大宫市开展初步调查，将该市作为高放射性废物最终处置场的潜在候选地点之一。
相关计划预计将提交给常陆大宫市政府。若当地接受该计划，常陆大宫市将成为日本第五个开展此类初步调查的地点。
日本高放射性废物处置场选址需经过多个阶段，整个遴选过程通常持续数年。此次拟开展的初步调查，是判断当地是否具备进一步评估条件的早期步骤。

title: 美国安塔瑞斯入选能源部核能发射平台计划
content:
美国安塔瑞斯入选能源部核能发射平台计划
安塔瑞斯公司(Antares)已入选美国能源部(DOE)核能发射平台计划。该计划由美国能源部核能办公室和国家反应堆创新中心(NRIC)牵头，旨在推动先进核技术从概念阶段走向商业部署。
此次入选进一步扩大了安塔瑞斯公司在得克萨斯州的业务布局。此前，该公司已根据美国空军“先进核动力设施计划”，被选中向圣安东尼奥联合基地交付微型反应堆。
安塔瑞斯公司首席执行官兼联合创始人乔丹·布兰布尔(Jordan Bramble)表示，反应堆试点计划加快了公司的发展，也深化了其与美国能源部和国家反应堆创新中心的合作。他说，核能发射平台计划是双方合作的自然延伸，也是为关键任务提供可靠电力迈出的下一步。
核能发射平台计划为开发商提供了相对简化的示范路径，以加快先进核技术的商业化部署。该计划依托美国能源部的授权和技术能力，为项目提供更灵活的技术与监管框架，推动相关技术从概念验证向实际部署转化。
通过“Launch Pad USA”路径，安塔瑞斯公司可获得美国能源部授权，在国家实验室之外运行核反应堆和燃料循环设施。同时，该公司还可获得爱达荷国家实验室(Idaho National Laboratory)及其他国家实验室的专业支持，包括核技术协助、能源部授权办理支持、灵活的合同安排，以及结合区域和项目特点配置资源的能力。
安塔瑞斯公司主要开发面向地面和空间关键任务的紧凑型裂变反应堆，设计目标包括工厂化生产和快速部署。2026年6月，该公司研制的Mark-0反应堆达到临界状态，成为美国40多年来首个达到临界的先进反应堆，也是美国能源部反应堆试点计划下的首个项目。核能发射平台计划将为该公司从示范阶段迈向部署阶段提供支持。

title: 日本埼玉市政府大楼花坛试用福岛去污土壤
content:
日本埼玉市政府大楼花坛试用福岛去污土壤
福岛第一核电站事故后产生的去污土壤，8月30日被运至日本埼玉市一处政府大楼，并用于现场花坛的再利用工程。
此次作业地点位于埼玉市中央区的埼玉新都心联合政府大楼。现场约有1立方米去污土壤被运入，工作人员在花坛内挖坑后，将土壤填入约20厘米深的位置，再在上方覆盖约20厘米厚的普通土壤。
类似的去污土壤再利用作业已于29日在宫城县仙台联合政府大楼实施。除福岛县内的示范项目外，这是东京以外地区开展的第二个相关再利用案例。
作业当天，约50名反对此项安排的市民从早晨起聚集在现场附近表达抗议。

title: 印度与乌兹别克斯坦同意建立长期铀供应安排
content:
印度与乌兹别克斯坦同意建立长期铀供应安排
印度和乌兹别克斯坦8月30日在塔什干举行领导人会谈，决定将双边关系提升为全面战略伙伴关系，并同意建立乌兹别克斯坦向印度长期供应铀的安排，以加强两国在民用核能领域的合作。
印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪 (Narendra Modi) 与乌兹别克斯坦总统沙夫卡特·米尔济约耶夫 (Shavkat Mirziyoyev) 会谈后表示，双方将建立长期铀供应安排。相关安排的具体规模、期限和执行机制尚未公布。印度近年来持续推动核燃料来源多元化，乌兹别克斯坦是中亚重要铀资源国。资料显示，两国曾于2019年签署长期铀矿精矿供应合同。
除核能合作外，双方还设定目标，到2030年将双边贸易额提升至50亿美元。目前，两国贸易额已超过10亿美元。莫迪表示，双方将以系统化方式处理市场准入、银行服务、支付系统和互联互通等问题，为扩大贸易和投资创造条件。
此次会谈还涉及关键矿产、采矿、基础设施、农业、医药卫生、信息技术、数字公共基础设施、教育、文化和旅游等领域。双方签署了多项合作文件，并计划建立由外交部长组成的协调委员会，以统筹推进各领域合作。现有联合委员会也将由秘书级提升至部长级。
在地方合作和城市发展方面，印度和乌兹别克斯坦正推进三项友好城市和友好邦协议。莫迪还提到，乌兹别克斯坦正在推进“新塔什干”建设，印度愿接待乌方代表团考察古吉拉特邦国际金融科技城 (GIFT City) 的规划和技术应用经验。
乌方表示，将围绕能源、文化、关键矿产、医药、珠宝和农业等重点领域制定路线图，并通过互派团队明确合作目标。米尔济约耶夫还表示，乌兹别克斯坦计划对印度公民实施30天以内免签入境安排，以促进旅游、商务往来和民间交流。

title: 韩国在美国举办韩美核工业合作研讨会
content:
韩国核能出口工业协会
NECX 2026
韩国核能出口工业协会 (KNA) 8月30日表示，该协会已于27日在美国得克萨斯州达拉斯举办“韩美核工业合作研讨会”。
本次研讨会与北美大型核能活动“NECX 2026”同期举行，主要目的在于巩固韩美核工业合作基础，并为韩国企业进入美国市场、参与相关核能项目创造对接机会。
约70名来自韩美两国核工业领域的代表参加会议。与会人员包括由韩国电力公社 (KEPCO) 和韩国水力原子能公司 (KHNP) 组成的韩国代表团、韩国中小企业代表，以及美国相关州政府机构代表。

title: 韩国KNR系统完成加压重水堆退役机器人系统开发
content:
韩国KNR系统完成加压重水堆退役机器人系统开发
韩国KNR系统公司 (KNR Systems) 8月31日宣布，已完成一套用于加压重水堆 (PHWR) 放射性结构远程切割与拆卸的平台系统开发，并计划于今年9月启动最终交付。
该系统来自一项由政府委托的加压重水堆退役示范项目。项目金额约28亿韩元，于去年1月授标，研发周期约7个月。交付后，相关设备将安装在韩国原子能研究院 (KRID) 庆州分院的重水反应堆退役技术中心，用于加压重水堆退役示范。
与轻水堆相比，加压重水堆内部结构更复杂，放射性污染水平通常更高，拆卸作业难度也更大。目前，针对商用加压重水堆堆芯结构开展远程切割和拆卸的机器人系统示范案例仍较少。KNR系统公司此次开发的平台，主要面向反应堆内部人员难以直接进入区域的结构拆除作业。
整套系统由四个部分组成：用于精确切割并取出反应堆内部结构的水平拆卸系统，用于拆卸大型结构并转运放射性废物的垂直拆卸系统，用于搬运拆卸物的重型起重系统，以及用于拆除排管容器 (calandria) 周边结构的穹顶结构拆卸系统。
其中，核心设备为重型双臂机器人。每条机械臂均采用7自由度设计，设备高度约2.4米，工作半径约2.5米，单臂最大负载可达400公斤。公司称，该机器人采用“超人形”设计思路，在搬运大型结构件时可实现类似人工操作的精细动作。
该系统的驱动方案采用KNR系统公司过去25年积累的液压精密控制技术。公司表示，与电机驱动相比，液压驱动在单位体积内可输出更高功率，同时减少对电子元件的依赖，更适合辐射、高温、粉尘等极端环境下的核设施退役作业。
系统还集成了智能液压控制和数字孪生仿真技术，具备防尘、防水、耐热、抗震和抗辐射能力，可在水下环境中进行精准远程控制。KNR系统公司计划以此次示范为基础，参与韩国国内核电站退役项目，并进一步开拓海外市场。
韩国正在推进或研究轻水堆和重水堆的受控区域退役工作，涉及古里1号机组、月城1号机组等项目。从长期看，加拿大、阿根廷、罗马尼亚、中国、印度等拥有加压重水堆运行经验的国家，也被视为相关退役技术的潜在市场。
核电站退役通常包括永久关闭、退役计划审批、乏燃料移出、放射性系统和构筑物拆除以及场地恢复等环节。此次开发的机器人系统主要用于放射性构筑物拆除阶段，这也是退役过程中技术难度较高的环节之一。
KNR系统公司首席执行官金明汉 (Kim Myung-han) 表示，利用国产技术在7个月内完成核电站退役机器人研发，说明相关机器人设计和控制技术能够适用于高难度作业环境。公司还在开发面向极端环境的其他机器人，包括用于重型作业的超人形机器人和1吨级四足机器人。

title: 印度塔塔咨询工程公司呼吁扩大私营部门参与核能研发
content:
印度塔塔咨询工程公司呼吁扩大私营部门参与核能研发
塔塔咨询工程公司(Tata Consulting Engineers，TCE)董事总经理兼首席执行官阿米特·夏尔马(Amit Sharma)表示，印度原子能部(Department of Atomic Energy，DAE)应更加聚焦国家战略目标，并在核能发电相关领域与私营部门开展更深入合作。
夏尔马称，TCE与印度核计划合作已超过五十年。印度原子能部最初设立的核心使命是服务国家战略需要，而非直接承担发电任务。他认为，DAE可借鉴印度空间研究组织(Indian Space Research Organisation，ISRO)推动私营部门发展的经验，让企业在核能研发中拥有更充分的参与空间。
他表示，巴巴原子研究中心(Bhabha Atomic Research Centre，BARC)等科研设施可在合规前提下向私营部门开放，用于测试企业提出的核能技术概念。夏尔马称，中国、美国和韩国等国家已通过系统性安排推动类似合作。
在他看来，《可持续利用和推进核能以转型印度法案》(SHANTI法案)通过后，印度私营部门对核能领域的兴趣明显上升。该法案旨在处理核能项目中的责任等关键问题。夏尔马表示，在此之前，非国有企业不得开展相关核科学研究。
TCE认为，核能领域蕴含较大商业机会。夏尔马透露，公司正与JSW集团(JSW Group)、信实工业公司(Reliance Industries)和巴贾吉集团(Bajaj Group)等多家企业开展合作，推进复杂核电站项目的可行性研究及相关工作。
目前，核能业务约占TCE 300亿卢比收入的2%。夏尔马预计，随着私营部门参与度提升，到2030财年末，这一比例有望升至5%至6%。
对于大型核电项目，夏尔马认为，国有电力企业NTPC有限公司(NTPC Ltd)以及一至两家资金实力较强的企业集团可能具备承担能力。他表示，核电项目每兆瓦投资额超过300万美元，建设一座2000兆瓦级核电站约需60亿美元，因此只有少数机构能够负担此类投资。
他同时预计，市场对小型核电站的兴趣将增加，其中包括备受关注的小型模块化反应堆。按照他的判断，此类技术预计将在2031财年前后趋于成熟。200兆瓦至300兆瓦级核电站可能吸引自备电厂和数据中心运营商，后者近年来也在印度扩大投资。考虑到土地征用难度，现有火电厂改造为小型或中型核电站也可能成为一种选择。
夏尔马也提到行业仍存在若干关切。他表示，政府需要对核电站运行所需燃料的稳定供应作出承诺，这对计划在核能领域投入大额资金的企业至关重要。此外，印度还需要建立真正独立的监管机构，在现有原子能监管委员会(Atomic Energy Regulatory Board，AERB)基础上进一步完善监管体系。
除核能业务外，夏尔马表示，TCE已在数据中心领域与五家客户合作，并参与六个半导体项目。不过，由于相关业务中不少工作复杂度较低、商品化程度较高，未来未必会成为公司的主要收入来源。
受全球客户投资意愿下降影响，TCE预计2027财年收入增速将降至14%至16%。随着对美国CDI工程解决方案公司(CDI Engineering Solutions)的整合完成，公司预计2027财年营业利润率将由12.5%提高至13%至14%。目前，TCE拥有约8500名员工，并将继续每年通过校园招聘吸纳500多名应届毕业生。

title: 乌克兰推进敖德萨放射性废物管理系统现代化
content:
乌克兰推进敖德萨放射性废物管理系统现代化
乌克兰国家禁区管理署 (SAUEZM) 近日在敖德萨组织召开工作会议，围绕放射性废物管理系统现代化改造及相关国际技术援助项目实施进展进行讨论。会议在乌克兰国有专业企业“氡联合体”(Association Radon) 敖德萨跨区域分部举行，由乌克兰国家禁区管理署副署长奥列克西·布迪克 (Oleksiy Budyk) 主持，联合支持办公室 (JSO)、NT-Engineering 有限责任公司 (NT-Engineering LLC) 以及“氡联合体”管理人员和专家参加。
此次会议涉及两个国际技术援助项目：一是液态放射性废物运输设备的设计、制造、认证、供应、售后服务及操作培训;二是针对废弃密封放射源安全管理开展可行性研究。
根据项目安排，相关设备将用于从“氡联合体”跨区域分部储存设施中取出液态放射性废物，并将其运送至后续处理、整备和处置地点。项目还将梳理乌克兰在废弃放射源安全移除、运输和储存方面的设备需求与程序要求，涵盖现有储存设施中的非历史遗留放射性废物、正在使用并未来可能移交储存的密封放射源，以及受事故或冲突影响的放射源等。
会议期间，与会专家实地了解了敖德萨跨区域分部放射性废物储存设施的运行和储存系统，对相关设施进行了初步调查，整理了项目实施所需的基础数据，并讨论了后续工作安排。
乌克兰国家禁区管理署表示，项目实施后，将有助于清除液态放射性废物，释放相关储存设施，为后续退役工作创造条件;同时将推动现有基础设施改造和物资技术基础升级，提高废弃电离辐射源等放射性废物的管理能力。
减少放射性废物累积量、提升放射性废物管理设施安全水平，是相关机构当前推进项目建设的重要目标。

title: 日本东京电力将废止原子能改革监督委员会
content:
日本东京电力将废止原子能改革监督委员会
东京电力控股公司 (Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings, TEPCO HD) 8月27日宣布，公司董事会当天决定，将于2026年9月30日废止原子能改革监督委员会。
该委员会成立于2012年9月，由日本国内外专家组成，是东京电力董事会的咨询机构。其设立目的，是从外部视角对东京电力控股公司推进核电站运营组织改革的相关工作进行监督和审查，推动公司建设具备高水平安全意识、技术能力以及社会沟通能力的核电站运营体系。
东京电力表示，委员会成立以来，委员们依托专业知识和经验开展讨论，为公司推进核安全改革作出了重要贡献。鉴于该委员会受托承担的目标和职责已基本实现，公司决定结束其活动并予以废止。
东京电力称，今后将继续把委员会此前提出的建议和意见用于公司核电改革工作，并推动相关工作持续改进。

title: 韩国尤金MS获114亿韩元ITER核心部件订单
content:
韩国尤金MS获114亿韩元ITER核心部件订单
韩国尤金MS公司 (Eugene MS) 8月31日表示，已与韩国聚变能源研究院 (Korea Institute of Fusion Energy，KFE) 签订合同，将生产并供应第二批国际热核聚变实验堆 (ITER) 真空容器端口密封法兰。
该合同金额约为114亿韩元，相当于尤金MS公司2025年259亿韩元收入的约44%。合同期限截至2030年12月。根据安排，相关密封法兰将分三批交付给ITER国际组织，最终检验及相关程序计划在2031年6月30日前完成。
ITER真空容器端口密封法兰由大型紧固件等部件组成，主要用于固定端口塞，并对真空容器端口进行密封。该部件位于真空容器与外部系统的边界，是防止泄漏、维持真空容器超高真空环境的关键部件。ITER真空容器内部容积约为1400立方米，对边界密封性能要求极高。
此次第二批密封法兰将覆盖ITER从研究运行启动阶段，到第一次氘氚运行和第二次氘氚运行的整个运行周期，应用范围包括真空容器17个赤道端口和3个下部端口，共20个端口开口。
本次招标采用技术导向型评估方式，综合技术评估和价格评估结果确定中标方。其中，技术评估权重为70%，价格评估权重为30%，且仅技术评估平均得分达到85%及以上的企业具备入选资格。尤金MS公司凭借从设计、制造到检验和质量保证的全周期执行能力，最终获得该订单。
尤金MS公司方面表示，此次项目将其ITER相关业务从组装设备供应，进一步扩展至VS线圈现场绕制和真空容器端口密封法兰等领域。公司计划继续围绕聚变发电设施建设所需的核心设备、专业制造技术和真空边界组件开展业务。

title: 印度核电扩张带动机械密封需求 西尔玛蒂克布局核级供应链
content:
印度核电扩张带动机械密封需求 西尔玛蒂克布局核级供应链
2026年8月29日消息，印度西尔玛蒂克公司 (Sealmatic India Ltd.) 正在依托自主机械密封技术和核应用质量认证，拓展印度核能装备配套市场。随着印度推进核电装机扩张，反应堆及相关泵送系统对高可靠性机械密封件的需求预计将持续增加。
机械密封件虽不属于反应堆、泵、汽轮机等大型主设备，但在核电站安全、可靠和连续运行中承担关键作用。相关产品主要用于主冷却剂、反应堆冷却剂、辅助给水和应急堆芯冷却泵等系统，对密封可靠性、运行完整性和长期稳定性要求较高。
与普通工业机械密封相比，核电用机械密封进入供应链前通常需要经过专门工程设计、严格试验、资质鉴定和审批流程。西尔玛蒂克已获得 ISO 19443 核应用质量管理体系认证。该标准面向核能供应链，对质量管理和安全相关要求提出了更高标准。
印度目前核电装机容量约为8.8吉瓦，计划到2032年增至约22吉瓦，并提出未来20年达到100吉瓦核电装机容量的长期目标。随着相关项目推进，核电专用机械密封件及其他关键部件的需求有望扩大。
西尔玛蒂克表示，公司已开始为关键核应用供应国产机械密封件。不过，核电项目普遍存在测试、鉴定、调试和执行周期较长的特点，研发及供货机会转化为收入仍需时间。
在印度原子能部 (DAE) 和印度核电有限公司 (NPCIL) 的指导下，西尔玛蒂克正开发面向印度核工业需求的自主机械密封产品。公司称，在获得一项重要开发订单后，还在投入研发适用于未来核电站的其他密封件类型。
除印度国内市场外，西尔玛蒂克也在与欧洲设备制造商洽谈合作，寻求将核级密封技术推向国际市场。公司核能销售助理副总裁蒂鲁马莱·钱德兰 (Thirumalai Chandran) 表示，印度核电扩张为专业工程和零部件制造商带来长期机会，机械密封件体积虽小，但其可靠性对关键泵送系统安全连续运行至关重要。
西尔玛蒂克同时强调，核能只是其工业业务的一部分。公司产品还应用于石油天然气、炼油、石化、化工、化肥、制药、火电、船舶、纸浆造纸、航空航天、食品饮料等行业，并关注太阳能、工业扩张、水利基础设施和数据中心冷却等市场。公司称，凭借核级认证、本土技术研发和多行业布局，未来将继续拓展国内外核能及高端工业密封业务。

青海油田新能源年发电量超8亿千瓦时--中国能源新闻网

青海油田新能源年发电量超8亿千瓦时
今年年初以来，青海油田抓住高原清洁能源发展的机遇，坚持规模与效益双向并重，健全项目全生命周期管理与独立核算机制，全力推动已建项目稳运行、在建项目快推进，聚力打造低碳零碳采油气厂，以澎湃的绿能助力构建“油气新”三业协同、并驾齐驱的新发展格局。截至8月28日，该油田新能源发电量达8.1亿千瓦时，同比增长16.5%。
针对格尔木燃机电站的运营困境，青海油田依托精细化运营攻坚外部供能赛道，通过落地专项生产运营保障方案、优化运维作业流程、常态化开展机组检修管控，确保机组随时能够稳定启运。同时，主动对接多方主体，持续优化调度运行模式，通过推进设备节能改造等多项举措深挖降本潜力。截至8月28日，该电站今年完成发电量2.2亿千瓦时，在保障电网调峰任务的前提下，实现效益最优运行。
面对复杂的电力市场环境与消纳难题，青海油田凯驰光伏电站坚持量价齐升，持续提升光伏项目收益。该电站健全电力交易管理制度，建立日复盘、周分析、月总结的常态化工作机制，抓实长协签约、绿证交易、合同电量转让等业务，拓宽省间、省内双向交易渠道。同时，依托数字化技术升级光功率预测系统，科学调整设备养护周期，持续提升发电效能，实现电量、收益双向突破。
青海油田同步深挖内部节能降碳潜力，全面摸排23家用能单位、2000余台生产设备的能耗情况，推行“一厂一策”精准管控。针对6个已建清洁替代项目，该油田编制了生产运营保障方案和巡检维护标准，形成“1+N”清洁替代生产管理体系，持续提升运维质效。同时，加大技术革新提效力度，从强化远程监控、升级调控系统、优化工艺流程、高效设备维护等4个方向发力，加快推进数智化管控及工艺技术迭代升级。截至8月28日，该油田清洁替代项目的发电量、节气量同比分别增长30.1%、76.8%，累计减碳4.6万吨，项目实现整体盈利。（

title: 科学网-OpenClaw史上最大更新发布，从简化安装流程开始
content:
OpenClaw史上最大更新发布，从简化安装流程开始
迎来重磅更新的OpenClaw 2.0简化了安装过程，并加入新的共享云会话功能。
当地时间8月30日，OpenClaw宣布迎来“史上最大更新”，由933位贡献者（包含569位首次贡献者）共同完成，共计合并了超过1.6万个拉取请求（PR），占OpenClaw历史累计合并PR量的近50%。
OpenClaw方面解释道，在本次更新之前，团队在230天内发布了106个版本，而在将近7周内没再发布新的版本，根本原因在于：随着团队规模不断扩大，剧增的工作量与开发节奏逐渐超出了OpenClaw原有的技术底层以及发版流程所能承载的极限。于是，团队决定将代码架构与发布流程同步进行彻底重构。
对于新用户来说，OpenClaw 2.0在安装上的简化可谓是一大好消息。该版本降低首次安装门槛，直接复用用户电脑现有的条件（如 ChatGPT/Claude订阅、API Keys或本地模型），大量烦琐配置被精简或移出初始步骤，用户可以通过直接与Claw对话来完成后续设定。
同时，OpenClaw 2.0为用户带来原生网页体验，对用户接触最多的网页端进行彻底重构，打开网页即直接进入对话界面，方便实时追踪任务与后续配置。
在能力进化方面，Claw可以从简单的实用任务起步，并且能够无缝打通更多跨应用场景。例如：当家人发消息询问买给父亲的iPad型号时，只需告诉Claw“去查邮件里的收据并直接回复他”，Claw即可全自动完成。
团队还为该版本加入了共享云端会话功能，任务可以无缝转交或邀请成员加入，且上下文不会丢失。团队表示，这让OpenClaw从单人工具进化为可跨团队、跨家庭协作的“多人软件”。
安全防护也成为OpenClaw 2.0的重点攻坚方向。新版本引入了私密凭据请求机制，允许 Agent 通过掩码提示词请求敏感信息，而无需在对话历史或模型上下文中暴露具体的凭据数值。
此外，用户可选择开启代理防护功能，将受保护密钥的替换范围严格限定在已授权的目标地址，从而降低凭据因意外外发请求而泄露的风险。
团队总结道，OpenClaw“重构了人与软件的关系”：“软件不再是别人设计好、你只能被动接受的东西，而是变成了一个你可以指派任务、能围绕你的生活与工作进行塑造，并且真正属于你的存在。”
